title: Finding the Mustang's Jacking and Lifting Points
introduction:
I use the underbody drawing to locate the lifting areas along the sides of the car, then confirm the stamped triangle on the actual vehicle. The circled locations and enlarged views help you recognize those areas; the warning symbols mark the precautions that follow.

This overview identifies lifting points and equipment hazards. It is not a complete sequence for raising the car, positioning floor stands or lowering it. Before lifting, match the relevant precautions below to the equipment being used.

edits.why: The underbody illustration marks locations along both sides, with enlarged views showing the triangle-marked areas. I use the drawing for location and the vehicle's stamped mark for confirmation.

edits.text: WARNING: Find the triangle stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or vehicle frame to identify the correct jacking point. Raising the vehicle anywhere else can cause it to shift or fall and may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: The stamped triangle identifies the intended location; a nearby surface that looks substantial is not a substitute.

edits.text: WARNING: Never go underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. A jack can lower unintentionally. Always support the vehicle with floor stands; failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Lifting the vehicle and supporting it for work underneath are separate requirements.

edits.text: NOTICE: Use the jack supplied with the vehicle only for an emergency change of a deflated tire. Never use it to hoist the vehicle for another purpose, as vehicle damage may result.
edits.why: The supplied emergency jack has a specifically limited use.

edits.text: NOTICE: Never apply jack pressure to the front or rear bumper on any vehicle. Doing so will damage the bumper covers.
edits.why: The bumper covers are not jacking contact points.

edits.text: NOTICE: Before lifting, position the hoist adapters carefully so they do not damage the suspension, exhaust or steering linkage components.
edits.why: Adapter placement must account for nearby components as well as the intended support location.

edits.text: NOTICE: Before driving the vehicle onto a drive-on lift, check for interference that could damage the underbody.
edits.why: The clearance check belongs before the vehicle travels onto the lift.

edits.text: NOTICE: When positioning the vehicle on a two-column hoist, keep the hoisting forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped. Position the hoist carefully to avoid damaging the axle or rear cover as well.
edits.why: This equipment-specific check covers both fork interference and potential damage near the axle and its rear cover.
